components.heading: (a) Notice of Hearing as defined in
components.text:
8.2.4.1 (a) Notice of Hearing as defined in
Schedule "A" section 15.1 shall be served at least
fourteen (14) days before the holding of the hearing,
upon the member whose conduct is being inquired
into and upon any other person or entity upon whom
the Discipline Committee deems it necessary for their
purpose to serve a Notice of Hearing upon.
(b) Notice of Hearing shall state the
subject matter of the hearing, the time and place of
the holding of the hearing and shall be signed by the
Registrar, or the Secretary of the Association of New
Brunswick Land Surveyors.
(c) The testimony of witnesses shall be
taken under oath or affirmation, which the chairman
of the Discipline Committee or any person
designated to do so on his behalf, is hereby
authorized to administer, and there shall be full right
to examine, cross-examine and re-examine
witnesses.

components.heading: (d) (i) The Chairman of the Discipline
components.text:
8.2.4.2 (d) (i) The Chairman of the Discipline
Committee, or someone designated by him to act on
his behalf, and upon payment of the fees prescribed
in the Rules of Court, may issue a Summons to
Witness, in a form prescribed by Schedule"C"
Section 15.3, for the purpose of procuring the
attendance and evidence, verbal, documentary or
otherwise, of witnesses before the Committee by
signing the Summons to Witness and sealing it with
the seal of the Association.
(ii) Pursuant to paragraph 8.2.4(d)(1),
the Registrar of the Association shall issue a blank
Summons to Witness signed by him under the seal of
the Association and the party may complete the
summons and insert therein of the required
particulars.
(iii) A Summons to Witness shall be
served personally and service may be proved by
Affidavit.
(iv) A Summons to Witness continues to
have effect until the conclusion of the hearing for
which the attendance of the witness is required.

components.heading: The proceedings and penalties in the case of
components.text:
8.2.5 The proceedings and penalties in the case of
disobedience to any Notice of Hearing or Summons
to Witness shall be the same as provided for in
section 24.8 of the New Brunswick Land Surveyors
Act, 1986.

components.heading: On the written authority of the Chairperson
components.text:
8.2.6 On the written authority of the Chairperson
of the Committee any evidence to be used at a hearing
may be taken by affidavit and the Discipline
Committee may proceed and act upon such evidence
as to the whole subject matter of the hearing or as to
any particular fact.

components.heading: The Committee shall have all proceedings,
components.text:
8.2.7 The Committee shall have all proceedings,
hearings and evidence recorded, transcribed and
certified by an Official Court Reporter or other
shorthand reporter duly sworn for that purpose.

components.heading: At all hearings the burden of proof of the
components.text:
8.2.8 At all hearings the burden of proof of the
subject matter is the same as that in civil actions.

components.heading: It is the duty of the member whose conduct is
components.text:
8.2.9 It is the duty of the member whose conduct is
being inquired into to appear at the hearing, but in the
event of non-attendance of such member, the
Discipline Committee upon receipt of proof by
affidavit or statutory declaration, of the service of the
Notice of Hearing may proceed with the hearing and
without further notice to such member, make a report
of their findings or take such other action as the
Discipline Committee is authorized to take under the
Act and such member shall be bound by the report or
action of the Discipline Committee.

components.heading: Notwithstanding:
components.text:
8.2.10 Notwithstanding:
(a) any vacancy in the membership of the
Discipline Committee; or
(b) the absence of any member of the Discipline
Committee during any part of the hearing;
the Discipline Committee may conduct or continue
the hearing if a majority of the Discipline Committee
or the Executive Council is present.

components.heading: Professional Misconduct
components.text: 8.3 Professional Misconduct

components.heading: Professional Misconduct is defined as
components.text:
8.3.1 Professional Misconduct is defined as
follows:
(a) the conduct of a practitioner which, in the
opinion of the Discipline Committee, is detrimental
to the interests of the public and contravenes the
Canons of Ethics of the profession;
(b) the breach by a Land Surveyor of the
standards of surveying established by the
Association; and
(c) negligence, misrepresentation or any other
conduct which, in the opinion of the Discipline
Committee, renders a Land Surveyor unfit to practice
land surveying.
9. AWARDS

components.heading: George Sproule Award
components.text: 9.1 George Sproule Award

components.heading: The George Sproule Award shall be awarded
components.text:
9.1.1 The George Sproule Award shall be awarded
to a person or persons who, in the opinion of the
Association of New Brunswick Land Surveyors, has
exhibited an outstanding contribution in promoting
and/or advancing the profession of Land Surveying.
The award shall not be restricted to land surveyors
and shall not necessarily be presented annually nor
limited to one award annually.

components.heading: Surveyor-in-Training Award
components.text: 9.2 Surveyor-in-Training Award

components.heading: The Surveyor-in-Training Award shall be
components.text:
9.2.1 The Surveyor-in-Training Award shall be
awarded to a surveyor-in-training, who in the
estimation of the board of examiners has achieved an
outstanding level of excellence in the completion of
the Legal Survey Project Technical Report. This
award shall not necessarily be granted annually nor
restricted to one award annually.

components.heading: Association of New Brunswick Land
components.text:
9.3 Association of New Brunswick Land
Surveyors Scholarship

components.heading: The Association of New Brunswick Land
components.text:
9.3.1 The Association of New Brunswick Land
Surveyors scholarship may be awarded annually to a
New Brunswick resident enrolled as a full-time
undergraduate student in the Geodesy and Geomatics
Engineering program at the University of New
Brunswick.
Revised January 2025

components.heading: The criteria for the scholarship shall be
components.text:
9.3.2 The criteria for the scholarship shall be
established by the Executive Council. The scholarship
will be made on the recommendation from the
Department of Geodesy and Geomatics Engineering at
the University of New Brunswick. This scholarship
shall not necessarily be granted annually.
Revised January 2025

components.heading: The amount of the scholarship shall be
components.text:
9.3.3 The amount of the scholarship shall be
established by the Executive Council in accordance
with the financial means of the Association.
Revised January 2025

components.heading: ANBLS Scholarship Repealed January 2025
components.text: 9.4 ANBLS Scholarship Repealed January 2025

components.heading: Student Assistance Program
components.text: 9.5 Student Assistance Program

components.heading: Under the Student Assistance Program, the
components.text:
9.5.1 Under the Student Assistance Program, the
Association of New Brunswick Land Surveyors may
accept and administer funds received from its
membership and other interested parties for use in
assisting students, student societies, or faculty
departments engaged in the post-secondary study of
land surveying. Added January 2025

components.heading: Funds received under the Student Assistance
components.text:
9.5.2 Funds received under the Student Assistance
Program shall be accounted for separately from the
Association general operating funds.
Added January 2025

components.heading: Funds under the Student Assistance Program
components.text:
9.5.3 Funds under the Student Assistance Program
may be provided to students, student societies, or
faculty departments on an ad hoc basis. While the
dollar amount cannot exceed the Student Assistance
Program account balance, Executive Council has
complete discretion in both the dollar amount and the
criteria for funds provided in support of any given
initiative under this program. Added January 2025

components.heading: The Treasurer shall deliver an annual report of
components.text:
9.5.4 The Treasurer shall deliver an annual report of
activity under the Student Assistance Program.
Added January 2025
10. STANDARDS

components.heading: All members of the Association shall always
components.text:
10.1.1 All members of the Association shall always
conduct their practice of land surveying in
accordance with the Standards Manual.
Revised January 2019

components.heading: A proposed new standard or the amendment
components.text:
10.1.2 A proposed new standard or the amendment
or repeal of all or any part of the Standards Manual
shall be presented in writing to the secretary signed
by at least two members sixty days before an annual
general meeting, and the secretary shall, in the notice
of an annual general meeting or a special meeting,
include a copy.
Revised January 2019

components.heading: A proposed new standard or an amendment
components.text:
10.1.3 A proposed new standard or an amendment
or repeal of all or any part of the Standards Manual
shall be approved by a vote of the members at an
annual or special meeting of the Association.
Revised January 2019
11. QUALITY ASSURANCE

components.heading: To better serve and protect the public interest
components.text:
11.1.1 To better serve and protect the public interest
the Association will establish a Quality Assurance
Program under the general administration of the
Council who shall be responsible for defining all
procedures implemented under these by-laws.
Revised January 2019

components.heading: The Practice Review Committee shall
components.text:
11.1.2 The Practice Review Committee shall
manage the Quality Assurance Program on behalf of
the Council by identifying opportunities to enhance
the program to better address trending deficiencies in
the results of member survey plan and file reviews,
or to enhance the administration of the program itself.
The Practice Review Committee shall make such a
review and deliver such recommendations and advice
in writing as requested by the Council, but not less
than annually.
Revised January 2019

components.heading: Subject to the approval of the Council, the
components.text:
11.1.3 Subject to the approval of the Council, the
Practice Review Committee will prepare and keep
current a Manual of Quality Assurance Procedures to
be used in the implementation of the program.
Revised January 2019

components.heading: The Quality Assurance Program will apply
components.text:
11.1.4 The Quality Assurance Program will apply
equally to all members. It may also respond to
referrals from the Council.
Added January 2019

components.heading: The Council shall appoint a land surveyor
components.text:
11.1.5 The Council shall appoint a land surveyor
member, retired member or life member to the
position of Quality Assurance Manager. Responsible
to the PRC, the Quality Assurance Manager shall
carry out the duties and responsibilities as further
provided within these by-laws including the Quality
Assurance Manual.
Revised January 2019
Revised January 2021

components.heading: All Land Surveyor Members are required to
components.text:
11.1.6 All Land Surveyor Members are required to
participate in the Quality Assurance Program.
Added January 2021

components.heading: Any member who may not be able to comply
components.text:
11.1.7 Any member who may not be able to comply
with the requirements of the Quality Assurance
program because of health or other legitimate
reasons may apply to the Practice Review
Committee for an exemption from the program for a
specific time. The Practice Review Committee shall
review this request and make a recommendation to
Council.
Added January 2021

components.heading: Plan Validation
components.text: 11. 2 Plan Validation

components.heading: Every copy of each plan certified by a New
components.text:
11.2.1 Every copy of each plan certified by a New
Brunswick Land Surveyor must bear a Plan
Validation Stamp. For the Survey of exterior
boundaries of Canada Lands the number of the Plan
Validation Stamp will be noted on the plan in lieu of
the stamp.
Revised January 2004
Revised January 2019

components.heading: The Plan Validation Stamp will consist of:
components.text:
11.2.2 The Plan Validation Stamp will consist of:
(a) an image of a design approved by the
Executive Council; and
(b) a Plan Validation Number, which will be:
i) sold to a land surveyor member only at
the fee prescribed in section 4 and sold in
accordance with procedures approved by the
Executive Council; and
Revised January 2004
ii) consecutively numbered and referenced in
a plan database approved by the Executive Council
and maintained by the Association;
Revised January 2004
Revised January 2019

components.heading: Land Surveyors using Plan Validation
components.text:
11.2.3 Land Surveyors using Plan Validation
Stamps must file with the Association, on the twenty-first day of each month, a list of the Plan Validation
Stamp numbers used in the previous month. The
content and format of the list will be in a form
approved by the Executive Council.
Revised January 2019

components.heading: If any Land Surveyor and/or participating
components.text:
11.2.4 If any Land Surveyor and/or participating
member company is delinquent in his submission of
numbers to the Association as per 11.2.3, the
Secretary-Treasurer is authorized to withhold the sale
of Plan Validation Stamps to that member and/or
member company until such time as the delinquent
numbers are submitted to the Association. A member
may appeal in writing to the Executive Council any
decision made by the Secretary-Treasurer to
withhold the sale of stamps.
Revised January 2019

components.heading: No plans signed by a Land Surveyor member
components.text:
11.2.5 No plans signed by a Land Surveyor member
shall be exempt whether registered publicly or for
private use, except those plans which do not depict,
affect, or otherwise make reference to boundaries.
Revised January 2019

components.heading: Any plan which is updated or amended and
components.text:
11.2.6 Any plan which is updated or amended and
subsequently is used in an official manner, whether
previously validated or not, will be required to bear a
stamp to validate its use, except those plans which are
exempt under Section 11.2.5.
Revised January 2019

components.heading: Except for in the case of a plan database
components.text:
11.2.7 Except for in the case of a plan database
record having a “canceled” status, Land Surveyor
members must submit a corresponding PDF plan to
Service New Brunswick within sixty (60) days of
creating a record in the database.
Added January 2022

components.heading: If a Land Surveyor member is delinquent in
components.text:
11.2.8 If a Land Surveyor member is delinquent in
submission of a PDF plan to Service New
Brunswick, the ANBLS plan database administrator
will disable that member’s access to the plan
database module within PLANET until the
delinquent PDF plan is submitted to SNB.
Added January 2022

components.heading: In certain circumstances, Land Surveyor
components.text:
11.2.9 In certain circumstances, Land Surveyor
members may require more than sixty (60) days to
submit a PDF plan to Service New Brunswick. The
ANBLS plan database administrator may extend the
sixty (60) day deadline for member submission of a
PDF plan when requested. The decision to extend
such an accommodation rest wholly with the ANBLS
plan database administrator, who will base their
decision on the individual circumstances of the
request. Added January 2022

components.heading: Survey Review
components.text: 11.3 Survey Review

components.heading: The Quality Assurance Manager or auditors
components.text:
11.3.1 The Quality Assurance Manager or auditors
under the Quality Assurance Program may conduct a
review of job files and office records of land surveyor
members which may include field inspections and
office visits.
Added January 2019

components.heading: The Quality Assurance Manager or auditors
components.text:
11.3.2 The Quality Assurance Manager or auditors
under the Quality Assurance Program shall complete
a detailed report on each survey plan and file review
and provide a copy to the named member, to the
Practice Review Committee, and to the Council.
Added January 2019

components.heading: Following a survey plan or file review in
components.text:
11.3.3 Following a survey plan or file review in
accordance with 11.3.1, the Practice Review
Committee may provide advice or assistance or
recommend a program of upgrading to the named
member as directed by the Council. Added January 2019

components.heading: The standards and procedures to be applied by
components.text:
11.3.4 The standards and procedures to be applied by
the Quality Assurance Program are those identified
in the Standards Manual. Added January 2019

components.heading: Failure to comply with the quality assurance
components.text:
11.4 Failure to comply with the quality assurance
program.
Added January 2021

components.heading: Except to the extent excused in accordance
components.text:
11.4.1 Except to the extent excused in accordance
with section 11.1.7, and subject to section 11.4.2, a
member who fails to comply with the Quality
Assurance Program will have their right to practice
revoked.
Added January 2021

components.heading: Council, may, in its discretion and where
components.text:
11.4.2 Council, may, in its discretion and where
special circumstances exist, defer the revocation of a
member’s right to practice in accordance with
section 11.4.1 for such period of time and upon such
terms as Council deems reasonable.
Added January 2021

components.heading: At least 30 days before revoking the right to
components.text:
11.4.3 At least 30 days before revoking the right to
practice under section 11.4.1, the Secretary must
deliver to the member a notice setting out:
(a) The date upon which the revocation of their
right to practice will take effect.
(b) The reason for revoking their right to
practice.
(c) The means by which a member may apply
to Council for relief under 11.4.2.
Added January 2021
12. LIABILITY INSURANCE

components.heading: Professional liability insurance is mandatory
components.text:
12.1.1 Professional liability insurance is mandatory
for all land surveyor members and life members who
maintain the right to practice land surveying.

components.heading: The Executive Council may allow, upon
components.text:
12.1.2 The Executive Council may allow, upon
application, exemptions to those members not
engaged in the practice of land surveying in New
Brunswick.

components.heading: Those members qualifying for the exemption
components.text:
12.1.3 Those members qualifying for the exemption
must file with the Registrar a duly signed and sworn
affidavit outlining the reasons they should be so
exempted. Any change of status must be reported to
the Association Office immediately.

components.heading: Repealed
components.text:
12.1.4 Repealed
Repealed January 2006

components.heading: The minimum limit of liability insurance
components.text:
12.1.5 The minimum limit of liability insurance
shall be $250,000.00 per loss and $250,000.00 per
policy period. The deductible clause shall not exceed
the amount of $10,000.00.
Revised January 2006

components.heading: Members and/or firms who obtain
components.text:
12.1.6 Members and/or firms who obtain
Professional Liability Insurance in lieu of the Master
Policy must provide the Association with a copy of
their policy or certificate on or before January 31
every year in conjunction with the submission of the
“Annual Registration Form” to the Association. In
the event of non-compliance, the Association will
revoke the member’s or firm’s right to practice.
a) This policy must have a minimum requirement not
less than section 12.1.5 and must include a 10-day
cancellation notice to the Association.
b) The right to practice will be reinstated when the
conditions of 12.1.6 are met.
Revised September 2023

components.heading: Members employed by Government or
components.text:
12.1.7 Members employed by Government or
Government Agencies must provide the Association
a duly signed and sworn affidavit outlining their
liability coverage.
a) on or before January 31 every year in conjunction
with the submission of the “Annual Registration
Form”.
b) within 30 days of transferring to another
department or government agency.
Revised September 2023

components.heading: Each insured member and/or firm is
components.text:
12.1.8 Each insured member and/or firm is
responsible for notifying the Association of any
change to their certificates, or to their status.

components.heading: The Executive Council may appoint an
components.text:
12.1.9 The Executive Council may appoint an
Insurance Advisory Committee to evaluate the
Master Policy and investigate any and all claims
made against insured members.

components.heading: The Executive Council may, on the
components.text:
12.1.10 The Executive Council may, on the
advice of the Insurance Advisory Committee, refuse
to issue an insurance certificate from the Master
Policy to any member who is named in more than
three claims per policy year.
13. GENERAL

components.heading: The conduct of business at a meeting of the
components.text:
13.1.1 The conduct of business at a meeting of the
Association shall be governed by Robert's Rules of
Order.

components.heading: The Executive Council shall appoint an
components.text:
13.1.2 The Executive Council shall appoint an
Official Parliamentarian for all annual and special
meetings of the Association.

components.heading: The Association of New Brunswick Land
components.text:
13.1.3 The Association of New Brunswick Land
Surveyors shall be a member of Professional
Surveyors Canada. The Executive Council shall
appoint a member of the Association to serve as a
representative on Professional Surveyors Canada.
The term of the appointment shall be determined by
the Executive Council. The Executive Council is
authorized to pay the required fee to belong to the
Professional Surveyors Canada.
Revised January 2011

components.heading: The Association of New Brunswick Land
components.text:
13.1.4 The Association of New Brunswick Land
Surveyors shall be a member of the Canadian Board
of Examiners for Professional Surveyors (CBEPS).
The Executive Council shall appoint members of the
Association to serve on the Canadian Board of
Examiners for Professional Surveyors (CBEPS). The
term of the appointment shall be determined by the
Executive Council. The Executive Council is
authorized to pay the required fee to belong to the
Canadian Board of Examiners for Professional
Surveyors (CBEPS).
Revised September 2008
14. CANONS OF ETHICS

components.heading: As the keystone of professional conduct is
components.text:
14.1.1 As the keystone of professional conduct is
integrity, it is the duty of land surveyors to practice
the profession according to these Canons of Ethics.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will conduct his work to a
components.text:
14.1.2 A Land Surveyor will conduct his work to a
high professional standard always maintaining the
dignity and honor of the profession and protecting the
public interest.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will cooperate, on a
components.text:
14.1.3 A Land Surveyor will cooperate, on a
continuing basis, in extending the effectiveness of the
survey profession by interchanging information and
professional knowledge with his fellow professionals
and student surveyors and by contributing to the work
and objectives of the Association.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will not act as an expert
components.text:
14.1.4 A Land Surveyor will not act as an expert
except in areas where he has personal knowledge and
honest conviction.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will not sanction or sign in
components.text:
14.1.5 A Land Surveyor will not sanction or sign in
a professional capacity any work not executed under
his personal supervision and professional knowledge.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will exercise due restraint
components.text:
14.1.6 A Land Surveyor will exercise due restraint
in criticizing another surveyor's work or reputation in
public; recognizing there are professional forums for
such criticisms within the Association.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will guard against any
components.text:
14.1.7 A Land Surveyor will guard against any
conflict-of-interest situations by disclosing any
possible conflicts to his client and/or employer and by
always putting the honor of his profession before
personal gain.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will not compete in an
components.text:
14.1.8 A Land Surveyor will not compete in an
unfair manner with another land surveyor or mislead
his employers or clients with misleading information
or unprofessional advertising.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will not disclose
components.text:
14.1.9 A Land Surveyor will not disclose
information concerning the business affairs of clients
and employers without their consent.

components.heading: A Mandatory Continuing Education Program
components.text:
18.1.1 A Mandatory Continuing Education Program
will be established and administered by the
Association, facilitated by a Practice Review
Committee under the direction of the Executive
Council.

components.heading: All Land Surveyor Members, with the
components.text:
18.1.2 All Land Surveyor Members, with the
exception of life members, are required to participate
in the Mandatory Continuing Education Program.

components.heading: The purpose of the Mandatory Continuing
components.text:
18.1.3 The purpose of the Mandatory Continuing
Education Program is to assist in maintaining the
high standard of quality of services which members
provide:
• by encouraging members to engage in educational
activities which maintain and enhance
professional practice; and
• by increasing the participation of members in
Association activities.

components.heading: The Mandatory Continuing Education
components.text:
18.1.4 The Mandatory Continuing Education
Program shall include a credit system to be
established by the Practice Review Committee and
approved by Council.
Revised January 2019

components.heading: The Practice Review Committee will
components.text:
18.1.5 The Practice Review Committee will
determine the eligibility of courses and course types,
seminars, workshops, Association activities, etc. and
establish a point rating for each. The point rating
system will be based on the relevancy of the course
or activity to the Association and to the practice of
Land Surveying.

components.heading: The Practice Review Committee shall
components.text:
18.1.6 The Practice Review Committee shall
distribute a detailed list of possible course types,
seminars, activities etc. to participating members.
Members required to participate in the program may
recommend other courses, activities etc. to the
Committee. These will be reviewed and, if deemed
acceptable, will be included in the Mandatory
Continuing Education Program.

components.heading: The Association will maintain a current
components.text:
18.1.7 The Association will maintain a current
record of points accumulated by each member
required to participate in the Mandatory Continuing
Education Program.

components.text:

points using the “Annual Registration Form” and
submit it to the Association no later than January 31
each year.

the Executive Council. Added September 2023

components.heading: Requirement for Preparation of a Survey
components.text:
19.0 Requirement for Preparation of a Survey
Plan subsequent to boundary monumentation
Any Survey Plan of a property will be prepared
according to Section G-4 of the Standards Manual.
All surveys that result in monuments being placed
shall have a Survey Plan prepared according to
Section G-4 of the Standards Manual.
The exception to this is when the placed
monumentation is in compliance with existing
coordinated plans that are:
a) referenced to the ANBLS Plan Validation
Database, or
b) registered in the Registry Office or Land
Titles Office for the Province of New
Brunswick.

sections.heading: The members of the Association shall be
Land surveyor members shall be persons who:
sections.text:
2.1.2 Land surveyor members shall be persons who:
(a) Are entitled to vote;
(b) Are entitled to hold office; and
(c) Have the right to practice land surveying.
Added January 2019

sections.heading: Life members shall be persons who have been
sections.text:
2.1.3 Life members shall be persons who have been
land surveyor members for a total of at least twenty years
and have made substantial contributions to the
Association and/or the land surveying profession and
who:
(a) Are entitled to any and all notices from the
Association to which a land surveyor member would be
entitled;
(b) Are not entitled to vote unless holding office
and have met all MCE requirements;
(c) Are entitled to hold office; and
(d) Are not entitled to practice land surveying.
Added January 2019

sections.heading: Honorary members shall be persons who,
sections.text:
2.1.4 Honorary members shall be persons who,
through their close association with land surveying for a
period of over ten years, have contributed greatly to the
advancement of the profession and the Association and
who:
(a) Are entitled to any and all notices from the
Association to which a land surveyor member would be
entitled;
(b) Are not entitled to vote;
(c) Are not entitled to hold office; and
(d) Are not entitled to practice land surveying.
Added January 2019

sections.heading: Surveyor-in-training members shall be persons
sections.text:
2.1.5 Surveyor-in-training members shall be persons
who are candidates seeking admission or readmission as
a member of the Association and who:
(a) Are entitled to any and all notices from the
Association to which a land surveyor member would be
entitled;
(b) Are not entitled to vote;
(c) Are not entitled to hold office; and
(d) Are not entitled to practice land surveying
Added January 2019

sections.heading: Associate members shall be persons who:
sections.text:
2.1.6 Associate members shall be persons who:
(a) Have the following qualifications:
i. They are now or were qualified to practice land
surveying in any jurisdiction other than New
Brunswick.
ii. They have been engaged in work which is closely
allied to land surveying for a period of at least five
years; or
iii. They have been engaged in the teaching of
surveying for a period of at least five years; and
(b) Have the following rights, privileges and duties:
i. They are entitled to any and all notices from the
association to which a land surveyor member would be
entitled.
ii. They are not entitled to vote;
iii. Are not entitled to hold office; and
iv. They are not entitled to practice land surveying.
Added January 2019

sections.heading: Retired members shall be persons who:
sections.text:
2.1.7 Retired members shall be persons who:
(a) have been previously a land surveyor member; and
(b) they are entitled to any and all notices from the
Association to which a land surveyor member would be
entitled;
(c) they are not entitled to vote unless holding office
and have met all MCE requirements ;
(d) they are entitled to hold office; and
(e) they are not entitled to practice land surveying.
Added January 2019

sections.heading: Student members shall be persons who are
sections.text:
2.1.8 Student members shall be persons who are
enrolled as a full time, part-time or correspondent
student in a geomatics program or a related academic
program and who:
(a) are entitled to any and all notices from the
Association to which a land surveyor member would be
entitled;
(b) are not entitled to vote;
(c) are not entitled to hold office; and
(d) are not entitled to practice land surveying.
Added January 2019

sections.heading: Procedure on Complaint
sections.text: 8.1 Procedure on Complaint

sections.heading: A complaint regarding the conduct of any
sections.text:
8.1.1 A complaint regarding the conduct of any
member of the Association made by members of the
public or members of the Association shall contain
the information as per Schedule "B" section 15.2.

sections.heading: The report on investigation into the conduct
sections.text:
8.1.2 The report on investigation into the conduct
of any member of the Association shall contain the
information as per Schedule "D" section 15.4.

sections.heading: Procedure on Hearings
sections.text: 8.2 Procedure on Hearings

sections.heading: The Discipline Committee may employ at the
sections.text:
8.2.1 The Discipline Committee may employ at the
expense of the Association, legal or other assistance,
it considers necessary for the purpose of carrying out
a hearing or performing any of its duties.

sections.heading: The member whose conduct is being inquired
sections.text:
8.2.2 The member whose conduct is being inquired
into has the right to be represented by counsel, at his
own expense, at the hearings by the Discipline
Committee, or on the hearing of any appeal.

sections.heading: The Discipline Committee has the right to be
sections.text:
8.2.3 The Discipline Committee has the right to be
represented by counsel on the hearing or on any
appeal.

sections.heading: (a) Notice of Hearing as defined in
sections.text:
8.2.4.1 (a) Notice of Hearing as defined in
Schedule "A" section 15.1 shall be served at least
fourteen (14) days before the holding of the hearing,
upon the member whose conduct is being inquired
into and upon any other person or entity upon whom
the Discipline Committee deems it necessary for their
purpose to serve a Notice of Hearing upon.
(b) Notice of Hearing shall state the
subject matter of the hearing, the time and place of
the holding of the hearing and shall be signed by the
Registrar, or the Secretary of the Association of New
Brunswick Land Surveyors.
(c) The testimony of witnesses shall be
taken under oath or affirmation, which the chairman
of the Discipline Committee or any person
designated to do so on his behalf, is hereby
authorized to administer, and there shall be full right
to examine, cross-examine and re-examine
witnesses.

sections.heading: (d) (i) The Chairman of the Discipline
sections.text:
8.2.4.2 (d) (i) The Chairman of the Discipline
Committee, or someone designated by him to act on
his behalf, and upon payment of the fees prescribed
in the Rules of Court, may issue a Summons to
Witness, in a form prescribed by Schedule"C"
Section 15.3, for the purpose of procuring the
attendance and evidence, verbal, documentary or
otherwise, of witnesses before the Committee by
signing the Summons to Witness and sealing it with
the seal of the Association.
(ii) Pursuant to paragraph 8.2.4(d)(1),
the Registrar of the Association shall issue a blank
Summons to Witness signed by him under the seal of
the Association and the party may complete the
summons and insert therein of the required
particulars.
(iii) A Summons to Witness shall be
served personally and service may be proved by
Affidavit.
(iv) A Summons to Witness continues to
have effect until the conclusion of the hearing for
which the attendance of the witness is required.

sections.heading: The proceedings and penalties in the case of
sections.text:
8.2.5 The proceedings and penalties in the case of
disobedience to any Notice of Hearing or Summons
to Witness shall be the same as provided for in
section 24.8 of the New Brunswick Land Surveyors
Act, 1986.

sections.heading: On the written authority of the Chairperson
sections.text:
8.2.6 On the written authority of the Chairperson
of the Committee any evidence to be used at a hearing
may be taken by affidavit and the Discipline
Committee may proceed and act upon such evidence
as to the whole subject matter of the hearing or as to
any particular fact.

sections.heading: The Committee shall have all proceedings,
sections.text:
8.2.7 The Committee shall have all proceedings,
hearings and evidence recorded, transcribed and
certified by an Official Court Reporter or other
shorthand reporter duly sworn for that purpose.

sections.heading: At all hearings the burden of proof of the
sections.text:
8.2.8 At all hearings the burden of proof of the
subject matter is the same as that in civil actions.

sections.heading: It is the duty of the member whose conduct is
sections.text:
8.2.9 It is the duty of the member whose conduct is
being inquired into to appear at the hearing, but in the
event of non-attendance of such member, the
Discipline Committee upon receipt of proof by
affidavit or statutory declaration, of the service of the
Notice of Hearing may proceed with the hearing and
without further notice to such member, make a report
of their findings or take such other action as the
Discipline Committee is authorized to take under the
Act and such member shall be bound by the report or
action of the Discipline Committee.

sections.heading: Notwithstanding:
sections.text:
8.2.10 Notwithstanding:
(a) any vacancy in the membership of the
Discipline Committee; or
(b) the absence of any member of the Discipline
Committee during any part of the hearing;
the Discipline Committee may conduct or continue
the hearing if a majority of the Discipline Committee
or the Executive Council is present.

sections.heading: Professional Misconduct
sections.text: 8.3 Professional Misconduct

sections.heading: Professional Misconduct is defined as
sections.text:
8.3.1 Professional Misconduct is defined as
follows:
(a) the conduct of a practitioner which, in the
opinion of the Discipline Committee, is detrimental
to the interests of the public and contravenes the
Canons of Ethics of the profession;
(b) the breach by a Land Surveyor of the
standards of surveying established by the
Association; and
(c) negligence, misrepresentation or any other
conduct which, in the opinion of the Discipline
Committee, renders a Land Surveyor unfit to practice
land surveying.
9. AWARDS

sections.heading: George Sproule Award
sections.text: 9.1 George Sproule Award

sections.heading: The George Sproule Award shall be awarded
sections.text:
9.1.1 The George Sproule Award shall be awarded
to a person or persons who, in the opinion of the
Association of New Brunswick Land Surveyors, has
exhibited an outstanding contribution in promoting
and/or advancing the profession of Land Surveying.
The award shall not be restricted to land surveyors
and shall not necessarily be presented annually nor
limited to one award annually.

sections.heading: Surveyor-in-Training Award
sections.text: 9.2 Surveyor-in-Training Award

sections.heading: The Surveyor-in-Training Award shall be
sections.text:
9.2.1 The Surveyor-in-Training Award shall be
awarded to a surveyor-in-training, who in the
estimation of the board of examiners has achieved an
outstanding level of excellence in the completion of
the Legal Survey Project Technical Report. This
award shall not necessarily be granted annually nor
restricted to one award annually.

sections.heading: To better serve and protect the public interest
sections.text:
11.1.1 To better serve and protect the public interest
the Association will establish a Quality Assurance
Program under the general administration of the
Council who shall be responsible for defining all
procedures implemented under these by-laws.
Revised January 2019

sections.heading: The Practice Review Committee shall
sections.text:
11.1.2 The Practice Review Committee shall
manage the Quality Assurance Program on behalf of
the Council by identifying opportunities to enhance
the program to better address trending deficiencies in
the results of member survey plan and file reviews,
or to enhance the administration of the program itself.
The Practice Review Committee shall make such a
review and deliver such recommendations and advice
in writing as requested by the Council, but not less
than annually.
Revised January 2019

sections.heading: Subject to the approval of the Council, the
sections.text:

Practice Review Committee will prepare and keep
current a Manual of Quality Assurance Procedures to
be used in the implementation of the program.
Revised January 2019

sections.heading: The Quality Assurance Program will apply
sections.text:
11.1.4 The Quality Assurance Program will apply
equally to all members. It may also respond to
referrals from the Council.
Added January 2019

sections.heading: The Council shall appoint a land surveyor
sections.text:
11.1.5 The Council shall appoint a land surveyor
member, retired member or life member to the
position of Quality Assurance Manager. Responsible
to the PRC, the Quality Assurance Manager shall
carry out the duties and responsibilities as further
provided within these by-laws including the Quality
Assurance Manual.
Revised January 2019
Revised January 2021

sections.heading: All Land Surveyor Members are required to
sections.text:
11.1.6 All Land Surveyor Members are required to
participate in the Quality Assurance Program.
Added January 2021

sections.heading: Any member who may not be able to comply
sections.text:
11.1.7 Any member who may not be able to comply
with the requirements of the Quality Assurance
program because of health or other legitimate
reasons may apply to the Practice Review
Committee for an exemption from the program for a
specific time. The Practice Review Committee shall
review this request and make a recommendation to
Council.
Added January 2021

sections.text:

Brunswick Land Surveyor must bear a Plan

Executive Council; and

i) sold to a land surveyor member only at

Revised January 2004
ii) consecutively numbered and referenced in

sections.heading: Land Surveyors using Plan Validation

Stamps must file with the Association, on the twenty-first day of each month, a list of the Plan Validation
Stamp numbers used in the previous month. The

sections.heading: If any Land Surveyor and/or participating
sections.text:

member company is delinquent in his submission of
numbers to the Association as per 11.2.3, the

Revised January 2019

sections.heading: Any plan which is updated or amended and

subsequently is used in an official manner, whether
previously validated or not, will be required to bear a
stamp to validate its use, except those plans which are
exempt under Section 11.2.5.
Revised January 2019

sections.heading: Except for in the case of a plan database
sections.text:

record having a “canceled” status, Land Surveyor
members must submit a corresponding PDF plan to
Service New Brunswick within sixty (60) days of
creating a record in the database.
Added January 2022

sections.heading: If a Land Surveyor member is delinquent in

submission of a PDF plan to Service New
Brunswick, the ANBLS plan database administrator
will disable that member’s access to the plan
database module within PLANET until the
delinquent PDF plan is submitted to SNB.
Added January 2022

sections.heading: In certain circumstances, Land Surveyor
sections.text:

members may require more than sixty (60) days to
submit a PDF plan to Service New Brunswick. The
ANBLS plan database administrator may extend the
sixty (60) day deadline for member submission of a
PDF plan when requested. The decision to extend
such an accommodation rest wholly with the ANBLS
plan database administrator, who will base their
decision on the individual circumstances of the
request. Added January 2022

office visits.

and provide a copy to the named member, to the

Committee may provide advice or assistance or
recommend a program of upgrading to the named
member as directed by the Council. Added January 2019

program.

Assurance Program will have their right to practice
revoked.

sections.heading: Council, may, in its discretion and where

affidavit outlining the reasons they should be so
exempted. Any change of status must be reported to
the Association Office immediately.

Professional Liability Insurance in lieu of the Master
Policy must provide the Association with a copy of
their policy or certificate on or before January 31
every year in conjunction with the submission of the
“Annual Registration Form” to the Association. In
the event of non-compliance, the Association will
revoke the member’s or firm’s right to practice.
a) This policy must have a minimum requirement not
less than section 12.1.5 and must include a 10-day
cancellation notice to the Association.
b) The right to practice will be reinstated when the
conditions of 12.1.6 are met.
Revised September 2023

sections.heading: Members employed by Government or
sections.text:
12.1.7 Members employed by Government or
Government Agencies must provide the Association
a duly signed and sworn affidavit outlining their
liability coverage.
a) on or before January 31 every year in conjunction
with the submission of the “Annual Registration
Form”.
b) within 30 days of transferring to another
department or government agency.
Revised September 2023

sections.heading: Each insured member and/or firm is
sections.text:
12.1.8 Each insured member and/or firm is
responsible for notifying the Association of any
change to their certificates, or to their status.

sections.heading: The Executive Council may appoint an
sections.text:
12.1.9 The Executive Council may appoint an
Insurance Advisory Committee to evaluate the
Master Policy and investigate any and all claims
made against insured members.

sections.heading: The Executive Council may, on the
sections.text:
12.1.10 The Executive Council may, on the
advice of the Insurance Advisory Committee, refuse
to issue an insurance certificate from the Master
Policy to any member who is named in more than
three claims per policy year.
13. GENERAL

sections.heading: The conduct of business at a meeting of the
sections.text:
13.1.1 The conduct of business at a meeting of the
Association shall be governed by Robert's Rules of
Order.

sections.heading: The Executive Council shall appoint an
sections.text:
13.1.2 The Executive Council shall appoint an
Official Parliamentarian for all annual and special
meetings of the Association.

sections.heading: The Association of New Brunswick Land
sections.text:
13.1.3 The Association of New Brunswick Land
Surveyors shall be a member of Professional
Surveyors Canada. The Executive Council shall
appoint a member of the Association to serve as a
representative on Professional Surveyors Canada.
The term of the appointment shall be determined by
the Executive Council. The Executive Council is
authorized to pay the required fee to belong to the
Professional Surveyors Canada.
Revised January 2011

sections.heading: The Association of New Brunswick Land
sections.text:
13.1.4 The Association of New Brunswick Land
Surveyors shall be a member of the Canadian Board
of Examiners for Professional Surveyors (CBEPS).
The Executive Council shall appoint members of the
Association to serve on the Canadian Board of
Examiners for Professional Surveyors (CBEPS). The
term of the appointment shall be determined by the
Executive Council. The Executive Council is
authorized to pay the required fee to belong to the
Canadian Board of Examiners for Professional
Surveyors (CBEPS).
Revised September 2008
14. CANONS OF ETHICS

sections.heading: As the keystone of professional conduct is
sections.text:
14.1.1 As the keystone of professional conduct is
integrity, it is the duty of land surveyors to practice
the profession according to these Canons of Ethics.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will conduct his work to a
sections.text:
14.1.2 A Land Surveyor will conduct his work to a
high professional standard always maintaining the
dignity and honor of the profession and protecting the
public interest.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will cooperate, on a
sections.text:
14.1.3 A Land Surveyor will cooperate, on a
continuing basis, in extending the effectiveness of the
survey profession by interchanging information and
professional knowledge with his fellow professionals
and student surveyors and by contributing to the work
and objectives of the Association.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will not act as an expert
sections.text:
14.1.4 A Land Surveyor will not act as an expert
except in areas where he has personal knowledge and
honest conviction.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will not sanction or sign in
sections.text:
14.1.5 A Land Surveyor will not sanction or sign in
a professional capacity any work not executed under
his personal supervision and professional knowledge.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will exercise due restraint
sections.text:
14.1.6 A Land Surveyor will exercise due restraint
in criticizing another surveyor's work or reputation in
public; recognizing there are professional forums for
such criticisms within the Association.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will guard against any
sections.text:
14.1.7 A Land Surveyor will guard against any
conflict-of-interest situations by disclosing any
possible conflicts to his client and/or employer and by
always putting the honor of his profession before
personal gain.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will not compete in an
sections.text:
14.1.8 A Land Surveyor will not compete in an
unfair manner with another land surveyor or mislead
his employers or clients with misleading information
or unprofessional advertising.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will not disclose
sections.text:
14.1.9 A Land Surveyor will not disclose
information concerning the business affairs of clients
and employers without their consent.

sections.heading: A Mandatory Continuing Education Program
sections.text:
18.1.1 A Mandatory Continuing Education Program
will be established and administered by the
Association, facilitated by a Practice Review
Committee under the direction of the Executive
Council.

sections.heading: All Land Surveyor Members, with the
sections.text:
18.1.2 All Land Surveyor Members, with the
exception of life members, are required to participate
in the Mandatory Continuing Education Program.

sections.heading: The purpose of the Mandatory Continuing
sections.text:
18.1.3 The purpose of the Mandatory Continuing
Education Program is to assist in maintaining the
high standard of quality of services which members
provide:
• by encouraging members to engage in educational
activities which maintain and enhance
professional practice; and
• by increasing the participation of members in
Association activities.

sections.heading: The Mandatory Continuing Education
sections.text:
18.1.4 The Mandatory Continuing Education
Program shall include a credit system to be
established by the Practice Review Committee and
approved by Council.
Revised January 2019

sections.heading: The Practice Review Committee will
sections.text:
18.1.5 The Practice Review Committee will
determine the eligibility of courses and course types,
seminars, workshops, Association activities, etc. and
establish a point rating for each. The point rating
system will be based on the relevancy of the course
or activity to the Association and to the practice of
Land Surveying.

sections.heading: The Practice Review Committee shall
sections.text:
18.1.6 The Practice Review Committee shall
distribute a detailed list of possible course types,
seminars, activities etc. to participating members.
Members required to participate in the program may
recommend other courses, activities etc. to the
Committee. These will be reviewed and, if deemed
acceptable, will be included in the Mandatory
Continuing Education Program.

sections.heading: The Association will maintain a current
sections.text:
18.1.7 The Association will maintain a current
record of points accumulated by each member
required to participate in the Mandatory Continuing
Education Program.

sections.heading: Participating members shall report all MCE
sections.text:

points using the “Annual Registration Form” and
submit it to the Association no later than January 31
each year.

sections.text:

the Program on an annual basis and present a report to
the Executive Council. Added September 2023

able to comply with the requirements of the MCE
program because of health or other legitimate reasons
may apply to the Practice Review Committee for an
exemption from the program for a specific time. The
Practice Review Committee shall review this request
and make a recommendation to Council.

sections.heading: Requirement for Preparation of a Survey
sections.text:
19.0 Requirement for Preparation of a Survey
Plan subsequent to boundary monumentation
Any Survey Plan of a property will be prepared
according to Section G-4 of the Standards Manual.
All surveys that result in monuments being placed
shall have a Survey Plan prepared according to
Section G-4 of the Standards Manual.
The exception to this is when the placed
monumentation is in compliance with existing
coordinated plans that are:
a) referenced to the ANBLS Plan Validation
Database, or
b) registered in the Registry Office or Land
Titles Office for the Province of New
Brunswick.
Added January 2020

components.heading: Definitions
components.text:
Definitions

1 In this Act
“city” means a city within the meaning of subsection 22(2) of the Local Governance Act ; (cité)

“communication” and “communicate” mean any form of communication whether spoken, written or electronic; (communication) et (communiquer)

“court” means any court or administrative tribunal in the Province (tribunaux)

“Crown corporation” means a corporation that is accountable, through a Minister, to the Legislative Assembly for the conduct of its affairs, and includes a parent Crown corporation or a wholly-owned subsidiary; (sociétés de la Couronne)

“department” means a department as defined in section 1 of the Financial Administration Act ; (ministère)

“institution” means an institution of the Legislative Assembly or the Government of New Brunswick, the courts, any board, commission or council, or other body or office, established to perform a governmental function by or pursuant to an Act of the Legislature or by or under the authority of the Lieutenant-Governor in Council, a department of the Government of New Brunswick, a Crown corporation established by or pursuant to an Act of the Legislature or any other body that is specified by an Act of the Legislature to be an agent of the Crown in right of the Province or to be subject to the direction of the Lieutenant-Governor in Council or a minister of the Crown; (institution)

“linguistic community” means either of the English linguistic community or the French linguistic community of New Brunswick within the meaning of section 16.1 of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms ; (communauté linguistique)

“municipality” means a municipality within the meaning of subsection 1(1) of the Local Governance Act ; (municipalité)

“official languages” means the official languages of New Brunswick within the meaning of subsection 16(2) of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms ; (langues officielles)

“peace officer” means a peace officer as defined under section 1 of the Provincial Offences Procedure Act who serves the public, whether on behalf of the Province, a municipality or under a contract for the delivery of policing services with the Province or its institutions and includes a police officer as defined under that Act; (agent de la paix)

“publication” and “published” mean all forms of publication, whether paper or electronic;(publication) et (publier)

“public service” means those portions or divisions of the Public Service specified in the First Schedule of the Public Service Labour Relations Act that are prescribed by regulation.(services publics)

components.heading: Purpose
components.text:
Purpose

1.1 The purpose of this Act is the following:

( a)
to ensure respect for English and French as the official languages of New Brunswick;

( b)
to ensure that English and French have equality of status and equal rights and privileges as to their use in all institutions of the Province; and

( c)
to set out the powers and duties of the institutions of the Province with respect to the two official languages.

2013, c.38, s.1

( b)

( c)
evaluate this Act on a continuous basis and make recommendations for amendments,

( d)
advise institutions on measures to be taken to comply with this Act and meet the needs of the two linguistic communities,

( e)
provide support to employees of institutions and the public service to ensure compliance with language policies of the Province,

( f)
undertake public outreach initiatives, including regular consultation with stakeholders from both linguistic communities, to promote respect, understanding and communication between the two linguistic communities, and

( g)
perform any other duties assigned to it by the Premier.

2023, c.10, s.1

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN

2013, c.38, s.1

components.heading: Implementation plan
components.text:
Implementation plan

5.1 (1) The Province shall prepare a plan setting out how it will meet its obligations under this Act, and the plan shall include the following:

( a)
goals and objectives with respect to its obligations under this Act;

( b)
measures to ensure the equality of status of the two linguistic communities;

( c)
measures to ensure the equality of use of the English and French language in the public service;

( d)
measures to ensure that language of work is considered when identifying work groups within the public service and when developing language profiles for positions in the public service;

( e)
measures to improve the bilingual capacity of senior management in the public service;

( f)
measures to provide for the review and the improvement, when necessary, of the public signage policies of the Province, which policies shall include consideration of the two linguistic communities and of the linguistic composition of a region; and

( g)
performance measures for evaluating the effectiveness of the measures implemented under the plan and time frames within which they must be implemented.

5.1 (2) The Premier is responsible for ensuring central government coordination and oversight of the implementation of the plan prepared under subsection (1).

5.1 (3) Each portion of the public service shall prepare an action plan setting out how it will meet the goals and objectives included in the plan prepared under subsection (1) and how it will implement the measures included in that plan.

5.1 (4) As soon as practicable after the end of each fiscal year, each portion of the public service shall submit a report to the Premier with respect to the activities under its action plan.

5.1 (5) As soon as practicable after the end of each fiscal year and after receiving the reports under subsection (4), the Premier shall submit a report to the Legislative Assembly with respect to the activities under the plan prepared under subsection (1).

Language of the Legislature

Language of legislation

Equal authority of both language versions

Introduction of bills

Acts of the Legislature

Required publication in The Royal Gazette

Official documents

components.heading: Language of the courts

Language of the courts

16 English and French are the official languages of the courts.

components.heading: Right to use language of choice
components.text:
Right to use language of choice

17 Every person has the right to use the official language of his or her choice in any matter before the courts, including all proceedings, or in any pleading or process issuing from a court.

components.heading: Person not to be disadvantaged by choice
components.text:
Person not to be disadvantaged by choice

18 No person shall be placed at a disadvantage by reason of the choice made under section 17.

components.heading: Obligation placed on the court to understand language chosen
components.text:
Obligation placed on the court to understand language chosen

19 (1) A court before which a matter is pending must understand, without the assistance of an interpreter or any process of simultaneous translation or consecutive interpretation, the official language chosen under section 17 by a party to the matter.

19 (2) A court before which a matter is pending must understand both official languages, without the assistance of an interpreter or any process of simultaneous translation or consecutive interpretation, if both English and French are the languages chosen by the parties to the proceedings.

20 (2) A person who is alleged to have committed an offence within the meaning of subsection (1), has the right to be understood by the court, without the assistance of an interpreter or any process of simultaneous translation or consecutive interpretation, in the official language chosen by the person.

Publication of decisions

24 (1) Any final decision, order or judgment of any court, including any reasons given therefor and summaries, shall be published in both official languages where

it determines a question of law of interest or importance to the general public, or

( b)

Services provided by a peace officer

31 (1) Members of the public have the right, when communicating with a peace officer, to receive service in the official language of their choice and must be informed of that right.

31 (4) When determining if a peace officer has taken the measures necessary under subsection (2) within a reasonable time, a court shall consider the efforts made by the police force or agency to fulfil its obligations under subsection (3).

components.heading: Mandate and responsibilities of Commissioner
components.text:
Mandate and responsibilities of Commissioner

43 (1) There shall be an Office of the Commissioner of Official Languages for New Brunswick, as well as a Commissioner of Official Languages for New Brunswick.

43 (2) Subject to subsections (2.1) to (2.4), the Commissioner shall be appointed by the Lieutenant-Governor in Council on the recommendation of the Legislative Assembly, shall rank as and have all the powers of a deputy head of a department, shall engage exclusively in the duties of the office of the Commissioner and shall not hold any other office under the Crown or engage in any other employment.

43 (2.1) Before an appointment is made under subsection (2), a selection committee shall be established for the purpose of identifying persons as potential candidates to be appointed Commissioner.

43 (2.2) The selection committee shall be composed of

( a)
the Clerk of the Executive Council or a person designated by the Clerk of the Executive Council,

( b)
the Clerk of the Legislative Assembly or a person designated by the Clerk of the Legislative Assembly,

( c)
a member of the judiciary, and

( d)
a member of the university community.

43 (2.3) The selection committee shall develop a roster of qualified candidates and submit a list of names of qualified candidates to the Lieutenant-Governor in Council.

43 (2.4) The Premier shall consult with the leader of the opposition and the leaders of the other political parties having representation in the Legislative Assembly during the most recent sitting with respect to one or more qualified candidates from the selection committee’s list of qualified candidates.

43 (2.5) The Commissioner is an officer of the Legislative Assembly.

43 (3) Subject to subsection (4), the Commissioner shall hold office for a term of seven years and is not eligible for reappointment.

43 (4) The Lieutenant-Governor in Council may extend the term of the Commissioner for a period of not more than 12 months.

43 (4.1) The Commissioner may resign from office by notice in writing addressed to the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly or, if there is no Speaker or the Speaker is absent from the Province, to the Clerk of the Legislative Assembly.

43 (4.2) The Speaker or the Clerk, as the case may be, shall immediately inform the Lieutenant-Governor in Council of the Commissioner’s resignation.

43 (4.3) The Commissioner shall hold office during good behaviour and may only be removed by the Lieutenant-Governor in Council for incapacity, neglect of duty or misconduct upon an address in which 2/3 of the members of the Legislative Assembly concur.

43 (4.4) The Lieutenant-Governor in Council, upon an address in which a majority of the members of the Legislative Assembly voting concur, may suspend the Commissioner, with or without pay, pending an investigation that may lead to removal under subsection (4.3).

43 (4.5) If the Legislature is not in session, a judge of The Court of King’s Bench of New Brunswick may, on an application by the Lieutenant-Governor in Council, suspend the Commissioner, with or without pay, for incapacity, neglect of duty or misconduct.

43 (5) If the Lieutenant-Governor in Council makes an application under subsection (4.5), the practice and procedure of The Court of King’s Bench of New Brunswick respecting applications applies.

43 (5.1) If a judge of The Court of King’s Bench of New Brunswick suspends the Commissioner under subsection (4.5), the judge shall do the following:

( a)
appoint an acting Commissioner to hold office until the suspension has been dealt with by the Legislative Assembly; and

( b)
table a report on the suspension with the Legislative Assembly within ten days after the commencement of the next session of the Legislature.

43 (5.2) No suspension under subsection (4.5) shall continue beyond the end of the next session of the Legislature.

43 (5.3) If the Commissioner has been suspended under subsection (4.4), the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may appoint an acting Commissioner to hold office until the suspension has elapsed.

43 (5.4) An acting Commissioner, while in office, has the powers and duties of the Commissioner and shall be paid such salary or other remuneration and expenses as the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may fix.

43 (5.5) The Lieutenant-Governor in Council may appoint an acting Commissioner for a term of up to one year if

( a)
the office of Commissioner becomes vacant during a sitting of the Legislative Assembly, but the Legislative Assembly does not make a recommendation under subsection (2) before the end of the sitting, or

( b)
the office of Commissioner becomes vacant while the Legislative Assembly is not sitting.

43 (5.6) The appointment of an acting Commissioner comes to an end when a new Commissioner is appointed under subsection (2).

43 (5.7) If the Commissioner is unable to act because of illness, the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may appoint an acting Commissioner, whose appointment comes to an end when the Commissioner is again able to act or when the office becomes vacant.

43 (5.8) An appointment under subsection (5.1), (5.3), (5.5) or (5.7) shall not impede a person’s subsequent appointment under subsection (2).

43 (5.9) The Premier shall consult with the leader of the opposition before an appointment is made under subsection (5.3), (5.5) or (5.7).

43 (6) Notwithstanding the Civil Service Act , the Commissioner may appoint such persons to positions in the Office of the Commissioner as he or she considers necessary to enable the fulfillment of the Commissioner’s responsibilities under this Act.

43 (6.1) The Commissioner shall be paid an annual salary as determined by the Lieutenant-Governor in Council within the deputy head pay plan, and is entitled to receive benefits similar to those received by deputy heads.

43 (7) The pension plan converted to a shared risk plan in accordance with An Act Respecting Public Service Pensions applies to the Commissioner and the employees of the Office of the Commissioner.

43 (8) The Commissioner may contract for such professional services, for limited periods of time or in respect of particular matters, as he or she considers necessary to enable the fulfillment of the Commissioner’s responsibilities under this Act.

43 (9) In accordance with the authority provided to the Commissioner under this Act, it is the role of the Commissioner to investigate, report on and make recommendations with regard to compliance with this Act and to promote the advancement of both official languages in the Province.

43 (10) In order to fulfill the role under subsection (9), the Commissioner shall conduct and carry out investigations either pursuant to any complaint made to the Commissioner or on his or her own initiative and shall, as provided in this Act, report and make recommendations with respect to such investigations.

43 (10.1) Despite subsection (10), when the Commissioner considers it appropriate, the Commissioner may attempt to resolve a complaint without conducting an investigation.

43 (11) The Commissioner may refuse to investigate or cease to investigate any complaint if, in the opinion of the Commissioner,

( a)
the subject-matter of the complaint is trivial,

( b)
the complaint is frivolous or vexatious or is not made in good faith, or

( c)
the subject-matter of the complaint does not involve a contravention or failure to comply with this Act or, for any other reason, does not come within the authority of the Commissioner under this Act.

43 (12) If the Commissioner refuses to investigate or ceases to investigate any complaint, the Commissioner shall inform the complainant and provide reasons for the decision to do so.

43 (13) Before commencing an investigation under this Act, the Commissioner shall inform the deputy head or other administrative head of the institution concerned of his or her intention to carry out the investigation.

43 (14) Subject to this Act, the Commissioner may determine the procedure to be followed in carrying out an investigation under this Act.

43 (15) For the purposes of this Act, the Commissioner is a commissioner under the Inquiries Act .

43 (16) After carrying out an investigation pursuant to a complaint under this Act, the Commissioner shall communicate the results of the investigation and any recommendations, including any opinion and the reasons for the recommendations, to the Premier, the deputy head or other administrative head of the institution concerned and the complainant.

43 (17) After carrying out an investigation on his or her own initiative, the Commissioner shall communicate the results of the investigation and any recommendations, including any opinion and the reasons for the recommendations, to the Premier and the deputy head or other administrative head of the institution concerned.

43 (17.1) When the Premier, a deputy head or an administrative head receives the results of an investigation from the Commissioner under subsection (16) or (17), he or she shall acknowledge in writing receipt of the results and of any recommendations made by the Commissioner.

43 (17.2) After carrying out an investigation under subsection (10), if the Commissioner considers it to be in the public interest, the Commissioner may publish a report on the results of his or her investigation and on any recommendations made as a result of the investigation.

43 (18) If a complainant is not satisfied with the conclusions of the Commissioner received under subsection (16) or with the resolution of the complaint, the complainant may apply to The Court of King’s Bench of New Brunswick for a remedy.

43 (19) The judge of a court referred to in subsection (18) may grant such remedy as he or she considers appropriate and just in the circumstances.

43 (20) This section does not affect any other right of action that a person may have.

43 (21) As soon as is reasonably practicable after the end of each year, the Commissioner shall submit to the Legislative Assembly a report, prepared by the Commissioner, with respect to the activities of the Office of the Commissioner in the preceding year that includes the following information:

( a)
the nature of the complaints that were received;

( b)
the types of complaints that were received;

( c)
whether an investigation that was carried out was pursuant to a complaint that was made or on the initiative of the Commissioner; and

( d)
the number of instances a particular complaint was made by the same complainant.
